ADAMS GEN

A 15,360 × 15,360 m world (235,929,600 m²) with the fantasy highlands of Mistiria Falls, mountain ranges, fast rivers running off the ice, pine-covered slopes, oak and birch forests, and lakes lined with weeping willows. A new random world every time you load. Walk it, chop it, swim it, build on it.

W A S D
move, Mouse to look
Space / Shift
jump / sprint
F / Ctrl
toggle flying / descend
Left click
carve blocks into chunks (a shovel digs wider), mine stone for stone chunks with a pickaxe (stone can't be mined by hand; deep down, below about Y -60, dark hardstone takes many more strikes), pluck grass, pick up sticks, rocks and flowers, chop trees with an axe (hold)
Hold Left click
eat the mushroom in your hand (be careful, some are poisonous)
Spear
craft one from a rock, 2 sticks and a thread. Hold Left click to ready it (your body stays put, the view still turns), line a fish up in the crosshair and let go to strike. Pick the fish up from the lake bed. Or hold Right click to ready a throw and let go to hurl it: it flies in an arc and sticks where it lands (even in the lake bed), and Left click picks it up again
Clover
thick carpets of clover grow on the plains close to lakes, in small patches and big meadows. Usually three round leaflets with a pale chevron; now and then a four-leaf one turns up. Digging or building on a block clears the clover on it
Boulders
big rocks lie on the ground or sit half buried, from knee-high to several metres across: common in the woods, scarce on the plains. Strike one with a pickaxe, again and again, to break it down until it is gone. Stone gives Stone Chunks. Whitish granite hides inside and shows on the surface in patches, and gives Granite
Mistiria Falls
a large fantasy biome (about a fifth of the world). The ground is shina, soft purplish-blue blocks with a starry sparkle, over greenish-grey shina rock. There are no trees, lakes or surface caves, but caves run through the rock below. Walk in and the sky turns purple and the clouds go dark purple. A dry storm never ends here: thunder rolls and lightning strikes, a howling gale blows (no rain) and every plant streams in the wind. Its rivers run pink. Curly, thin-leafed pink Mistiria grass grows in plentiful patches like clover; pluck it for grass fibre. Lonely liche trees stand here: 20 m tall, very thin dark-purple trunks with bare branches and no leaves. Chop them like any tree for purple Liche Wood (an axe on a wood block cuts it into Liche Plank chunks; 6 chunks make a block, 3 small chunks make a bowl). Shina and shina rock dig like other blocks into chunks (a pickaxe works on them too).
Blanka
a rare, huge four-legged beast of Mistiria Falls, about four times the size of a boar grizzly, with a furry hide, a great orange lion's mane, red eyes, clawed paws and a swaying orange-tufted tail. It wanders slowly, but come within about 16 blocks and it roars and charges
Lich crows
very big blackish-purple crows with huge wings and green eyes that live around the liche trees. One without a nest plucks pink grass and carries it back to its tree to build a pink nest. One with a nest swoops on you as you walk by, snatches one item and flies home with it; you can see stolen items in the nest. Climb up and step into the nest to take them back
Rivers
long rivers are born on the ice patches and snowmelt springs of the mountains and flow downhill to the plains and on across the world, winding in wide curves for 6,000 to 13,000 blocks. They are 3 to 30 blocks wide, sunk in a ditch below the ground, and the wide ones split into small branching channels that reach other parts of the world. The water rushes (the current carries a swimmer along), splashes up along the banks and holds fish like the lakes do. The top bar shows the distance and direction of the nearest river
Liche lizard
a hostile night crawler of Mistiria Falls, common after dark: about 2 blocks tall and 7 long, purple skin over a white belly, swinging its long tail as it crawls. Its red eyes cast a red glow in the dark. Once it sees you it sweeps straight through you, turns and sweeps again until you fall. Stand 2 blocks or more above it and it cannot reach you; it only circles and hisses below. Hunt it with spear or knife: a head shot kills at once, the body takes 3 hits. At first light every lizard walks home to its nest ditch and curls up there through the day
Liche lizard nests
shallow ditches dug into the shina of Mistiria Falls where the liche lizards sleep through the daytime. Each ditch holds two to four big, oval Liche Lizard Eggs: click them to collect, eat them raw or boil them over a campfire. Come close and the lizard guarding them will sweep at you even in daylight. A 1-block tunnel mouth in the bottom of every ditch drops into a maze of 1-block-wide, 1-block-tall tunnels that winds under the biome and joins the nests together underground
Liquor shrub
very tall blue grass (about 4 blocks) that grows in single dense clumps in Mistiria Falls. Its stalks stand straight and arch outward at the top; walk right into it. Pluck it for plant fibre, then dig the shina block under it to find a Vega Blanka, a pink vegetable tangled in the roots
Pine trees
tall dark pines (22 to 30 blocks) cover the lower slopes of the mountains, in dense stands in some places and a few scattered trees in others, thinning out towards the snow line. They chop like any tree and drop pine cones you can pick up. Stab a pine with a knife (a stick and a stone) and about five minutes later yellow resin wells up from the dent and slowly creeps down the bark. Click the resin while holding a bowl to collect it
Knife and bowl
craft a knife from one stick and one stone, and a bowl from three small wood chunks. Left click a tree with the knife to stab it: the blade leaves a dent in the bark, and a stab into a pine makes it bleed resin after a while. Hold the bowl and click the resin to fill it a drop at a time (it holds 3)
Caves
dig down and you find caves under every kind of ground: winding noodle tunnels, dead ends, caverns, low flat chambers and tall ravines, some holding pools. They get darker the deeper they are. Where a river ends, its ditch runs into a small cave mouth with a short, low tunnel, a tiny chamber and often a pool
Hillside caves
on steep mountain slopes the rock opens in cave mouths of every shape and size: tall arches, wide low crawls, round portals, narrow fissures, lumpy holes, rock shelters under an overhang, twin doors and leaning triangles. The steeper and higher the slope, the more of them you find. Behind a mouth a tunnel runs into the mountain, splits, widens into chambers and drops down shafts and ravines, and a long deep branch sinks towards the underground caves, so one opening can lead to a whole system. Some chimneys reach the sky from inside. They get darker the further in you go: bring a torch
Algae
about one in five still, calm lakes is covered with a thin green mat of algae floating on the surface. Jump or wade in and it parts around you and drifts out across the pond; a sip of water or an animal drinking pushes a smaller hole. Slowly the mat closes up again
River sounds
walk toward a river and you hear its soft rushing fade in, getting louder the closer you are. Loose rocks and boulders gather along river banks
Mountain ponds
on the flatter ground of the mountain ranges small still ponds fill the hollows. Blackthorn shrubs, grass, long grass, stones, boulders and mushrooms grow on the grassy lower slopes too
Rocky hills
on the lower mountainsides, bare rock hills rise almost sheer: shelves that jut out from the slope, towers that stand straight up, thin fins and low knolls, in every size. A big one often carries a smaller one on top and another on that, so stacks of them climb the mountain all the way around. Iron ore shows in their walls, and their grassy tops hold pines
Iron ore
rusty peach nodules of iron sit inside the rock everywhere underground, from just below the soil down to the bedrock floor, in hardstone as well as stone. They don't follow the blocks: most are a single nodule or a small clump in one block, some are scattered patches across a few blocks, and long veins are rare. Look for them on cave walls. Strike the part of the block with the ore on it with a pickaxe to get Iron Ore; the plain stone around it gives Stone Chunks
Granite
big whitish, speckled patches of granite run through the rock underground all over the world, spreading across several blocks. Look for them on cave walls. Strike them with a pickaxe to get Granite
Iron tools
stone tools wear out after about 15 uses (watch the bar under the slot) and break. Beat Iron Ingots on the anvil and craft iron tools that last about 120 uses: Iron Axe (3 ingots, 2 sticks, 2 thread) cuts one clean straight slice through the trunk; Iron Pickaxe (3 ingots, 2 sticks, 2 thread) breaks off more stone per strike; Iron Shovel (2 ingots, 2 sticks, 1 thread) digs wider; Iron Spear (2 ingots, 2 sticks, 1 thread) reaches further than the stone spear and hits 1.5x harder, sometimes dropping a bear in one strike; Iron Knife (1 ingot, 1 stick) lands a full hit with every cut
Trays and plates
cut one Stone block into 6 Stone Trays, or one Shina Rock block into 6 Shina Stone Plates; beat 2 Iron Ingots into 3 Iron Plates. They are thin, very straight slabs almost a block wide. Right click one onto the top of a block to lay it down (stack up to 8), left click to take the top one back
Pottery
only Wet Clay breaks into chunks; plain and dried clay come off as whole blocks. Place wet clay chunks and small chunks to shape anything you like, no taller or wider than 2 blocks. Right click the piece with a full bowl of resin to seal it (the bowl empties); after about a minute and a half it dries into plain clay. Then left click it to take the whole piece as one Clay Ornament: each one keeps its own shape and never stacks. Right click it onto a block top to set it down, left click to pick it up again
Anvil and hammer
craft a heavy black iron Anvil from 7 Iron Slag (it does not stack) and place it like a block; break it to take it back. Craft a Hammer from 2 rocks, a stick and a fibre rope. Right click Iron Slag onto the top of the anvil, then strike it with the hammer 3 times to beat it into an Iron Ingot
Dye
right click any flower or lily onto the top of an anvil to lay it out, then hit it with the Hammer 4 times to beat it into Dye the colour of that flower. Every flower and lily gives a different colour, including a few extra shades, so between them you can beat out White, Light Blue, Pink, Light Pink, Yellow, Orange, Red, Deep Red, Purple and Magenta Dye. Left click the laid-out flower instead of hammering it to take it back unused
The Infected Tree
a rare, fantastical giant found in any biome: a roughly 70 m tall tree, thick at the base, narrowing partway up and thickening again near the top, with a dozen curving boughs buried under a dense cloud of pink blossom. It is solid. No ordinary tool can cut it down - only a Liganite Axe is strong enough, and each strike leaves just a small dent; after dozens of blows it creaks and falls. The fallen giant is chopped up for 64 to 96 Hardwood Chunks, the dark heartwood all furniture is made from
Diamonds
a very rare pale-cyan gem found only in the deepest rock of every biome, either alone or buried at the heart of a coal patch. Only an iron or Liganite Pickaxe can mine it
Fences and fence gates
2 planks and 1 stick make a Fence; 2 planks and 4 sticks make a Fence Gate, for every kind of wood and for hardwood. Fences join to each other, to gates and to solid blocks, and are too tall to jump. Right click a gate to swing it open or shut; left click takes either one down. Villages fence their fields
Hardwood and furniture
2 Hardwood Chunks make a Hardwood Plank. A Sofa is 2 cushions and 8 hardwood chunks, two blocks wide, in the colour of its cushions; a Chair is 1 cushion and 4 hardwood chunks. Right click a chair or sofa with an empty hand to sit on it, and press a move key to stand up. Tables: a Small Table (4 chunks, 1 plank, one block), a Large Table (8 chunks, 2 planks, two blocks long) and a Dining Table (12 chunks, 4 planks, three blocks long with turned legs). Furniture turns its front towards you and goes on top of a block (a carpet under it is fine); left click it to pick it up
Pantry
20 hardwood chunks, 1 iron ingot and 4 hardwood planks make a Pantry: a tall cupboard, two blocks high, with two louvred doors. It works like a chest but holds 40 slots on four shelves: right click it with an item to store it, or with an empty hand to swing the doors open and see the shelves. Left click an empty pantry to pick it up
Ladders
6 sticks and 3 fibre rope make 3 ladders. Right click the side of a block to stand one against it (or click the floor in front of a wall); click a ladder to add the next one on top (look down to add it below). Walk into a ladder to hold on: W or Space climbs, S or Ctrl goes down, and you don't fall while you hold on
Carpets
7 wool of one colour make a carpet, and every colour has its own shape, pattern and weave: a White braided round rug, a Pink heart sprinkled with roses, a Grey medallion rug with tassels, a Yellow shaggy sunburst, a Green mossy hexagon with a ring of leaves, a Brown kilim runner and a Skin plaid octagon. Lay one on a flat floor, or on a table top (dining tables too), and it turns to the way you face. Furniture can stand on a carpet; left click a carpet to take it up
Bomb Beetle
a low, hostile beetle that comes out at night in forests, plains, cherry blossom groves, mountains and the desert. It shuffles slowly toward you, and once it gets within about 2 blocks its eyes flare red and its body shudders apart before it detonates: a crater in the ground, nearby flowers gone, and a heavy hit of damage and knockback if you're still close - it gives no materials either way. A spear only bounces off its shell; a Stone Sword needs 8 hits to put it down before it can go off (an Iron Sword manages it faster, a Liganite Sword faster still)
Wraith Spider
an eight-legged hostile spider that prowls at night, with glowing purple eyes. From a distance it rears its spinneret and spits a web - get hit and you're slowed, with each extra hit stacking the slow further until it tops out; the slowness fades on its own if no more webs land on you. While you're webbed up it closes in eagerly to bite. A head shot kills it outright, the body takes 4 hits to put down. At first light it crawls off to hide until dark again
Liganite
a rare purple crystal ore embedded in the shina rock very deep (below y50) in the Mistiria Falls biome. It smelts on a campfire built over a Forge exactly like iron ore, then hammers into Liganite Ingots on an anvil the same way. Liganite tools craft from the ingots and work like their iron counterparts, with their own edge: the Liganite Spear knocks back whatever it strikes; the Liganite Sword has far more reach and damage than an iron sword and carries a special attack, Burst Edge (press R while holding it) that slams the blade into the ground, shattering the rock around you and dealing huge damage to anything caught in the blast, though it yields no materials; the Liganite Pickaxe has more durability than iron and mines a whole block in a single hit; the Liganite Axe cuts bigger, straighter slices and is the only tool that can fell an Infected Tree
Torch
a full bowl of resin, a stick and 6 plant fibres make a torch. Hold it to light your way: it burns like a campfire but with a shorter reach and a flame that slowly swells and fades. Caves are dark even at noon, and the further a place is from open sky the darker it is; break a block that lets the sky in and the daylight pours in from the hole
Cooking
light a campfire, then put a hard surface right above it: a block or a chunk of stone, hardstone, cobblestone, bricks or shina rock (soft or loose blocks like dirt, sand, gravel, snow, shina and wood don't work). Aim a hard block or chunk at the fire to set it above it. Right-click with any food (meat, fish, eggs, berries, Vega Blanka) to place it down anywhere, on the ground, on blocks or on chunks. Food lying on the surface above a burning fire cooks: after 30 seconds it starts to smoke, and after 2 minutes it is cooked. Click it to pick it up again. Cooked food restores twice as much as raw food
Forge and smelting
craft a Forge from 8 stone chunks and 2 gravel and place it on top of a block. It is a dark stone furnace 2 blocks tall that only smelts metal: put Coal or Sticks in the lower opening (right click the lower half), put Iron Ore in the upper opening (right click the upper half) and wait about 25 seconds per ore for Iron Slag, which you take out with a left click. Left click an empty forge to pick it up. Old forges built from stone shelves still work
Farming
Craft a Stone Hoe (2 sticks, 2 rocks, 1 thread) and right click dirt or grass to till the whole block: a grass block turns to dirt and gets a ridged bed with four pits. Craft Vega Blanka Seeds (3 from a Vega Blanka) or Caucas Seeds (3 from a Caucas) and right click a pit to plant. Vega Blanka needs about 3 days, Caucas about 2.5. Left click a grown Vega Blanka, or dig the block under a plant, to harvest. Wild Caucas grows in rare patches on the lower mountain slopes: only the green leaves show, so dig the block beneath. Eat it raw or cook it on a campfire for more hunger
Villagers
every base house has one villager, a man or a woman, and every family house a married couple and 1 to 3 small children in the loft, each with their own face, hair, build, clothes and sometimes a straw farm hat. By day they wander the village streets; at dusk they walk home, open their door, close it behind them and lie down in their bed until morning. They only exist near you (this version does not sync them in multiplayer)
Chests
craft a chest from 3 planks and 1 iron ingot; every wood type makes its own chest (oak, birch, pine, liche, savanna and the four cherries). Place it on top of a block. Right click it with an item in your hand to store that stack, or with an empty hand to open it: click a chest slot to take the item, click an inventory slot to store it. A chest holds 20 slots and shows what is inside it. Left click an empty chest to pick it up again
Roofs, windows and cushions
a roof is 2 planks and 3 grass fibre (one per wood type): a sloped block that rises away from you, so face two roofs towards each other for a ridge. Roof corners join two slopes where they meet: an Outer Roof Corner (2 planks, 3 fibre) for the outside corner of a hipped roof and an Inner Roof Corner (3 planks, 4 fibre) for a valley where the roof turns inward; face the corner diagonally and it rises away from you. A window is 4 glass: a frameless see-through pane across the way you face, with a shine on it. A cushion is 3 wool, in the colour of the wool: a quarter-block pillow you lay on top of a block, and click again to stack up to 3. Left click any of them to pick it back up. You walk up a quarter block without jumping
Plains village
rare, big and named: a dozen or more houses, a chief's hall, a shop, a smithy, a carpenter's, an herb garden and a barn around a plaza with a statue, wells, and one wall with one big double gate (click a handle in the middle to open a leaf). They sit in any biome that has wood and a village's blocks come from its biome. A sign board outside the gate shows the village's name. Craft your own sign board from 3 planks, 2 sticks and a rope; right click to carve it. The compass line shows the nearest village
Coal
coal ore is found as black nodules in stone around river ditches and in the deeper caves; mine it with a pickaxe. Right click Coal onto a lit campfire to make it burn for 300 more seconds per piece
Lowlander's Hut
the first structure of the world. It stands at the very heart of Mistiria Falls, the spot that lies farthest from every other biome. Its walls are Shina Bricks under a stepped roof of Liche Planks, with a Liche door and a cold, ashed campfire outside. Inside there is a Liche Chest, and a sheet of Parchment Paper lies on the floor: a soft, cloth-like paper sheet you can pick up (left click it)
Forest Mushroom Golem
place four shina rock chunks in a T: one chunk standing on the ground with a bar of three chunks on top of it. Set a Black Trumpet on the middle chunk of the bar and the stones wake up as a little golem, one block tall, with a stony body, grass on top and the trumpet on its head. It follows you around. The Parchment Paper from the Lowlander's Hut tells how (right-click while holding it to read it), but you can build one without reading it
Morel Golem
place four plain stone chunks in a T: one chunk standing on the ground with a bar of three chunks on top of it. Set a Morel on the middle chunk of the bar and the stones shudder into a sharper, dark blue golem with a boxy head, mushroom antennae, arms held out in a T, little legs and a turfy head with the morel growing on it. It follows you around. The Parchment Paper in the Lowlander's Hut gives one of the two golem recipes, picked at random for each world
Shina stone
shina rock can only be mined with a pickaxe. 4 shina rock chunks craft a block of Shina Bricks, which you place and break like any block (you get the whole block back). 2 chunks craft a Shina Stone Pole: a thin post one block tall that stands on a block top; click it to take it back
Dysentery
drinking still lake or pond water makes you sick about 10 s later: your health drains steadily for 1.5 to 3 min and you get thirsty 2.5x faster. River water is safe. Mushroom stew cures it.
Ague
sleeping in the open, within 20 blocks of a still pond or lake with no lit fire (campfire or furnace) within 4 blocks, can give you ague for 2 to 9 days. Cold chills (slow, no sprinting, health loss) and fevers (thirst) come in waves with rests between. Sleep by a fire to stay safe.
Salmonella
raw meat of land animals and birds (not fish) gives you salmonella a few seconds later for 1 to 3 min: you lose health and your hunger bar empties faster. Cook your meat.
Fall damage
drops of up to 3 blocks are harmless. Beyond that you lose health the further you fall: with full health you survive a 10-block fall and any more kills you. When you are hurt the deadly height drops (at half health about 6 blocks). Water breaks your fall.
Stamina
at first you can run for only 40 s before you must walk for 3 min to recover. Run at least a minute every day and your stamina grows (see the Stats tab in your inventory). You can skip up to 3 days in a row; more than that and it fades. At the very top you can run for 10 min and need only 1 min to recover, which takes a very long time.
Snow peaks
the tallest ranges climb towards Y 1000. Snow starts in patches around Y 450 and gets deeper and wider up to 650; above 850 the whole mountain is white. Snow carves into Snow chunks by hand, but a shovel scoops it in big bites. Above Y 780 there are patches of ice: scrape it into Ice chunks (a shovel works best) and watch your step, it is slippery. 6 chunks craft a block, 4 snow blocks pack into ice
Flowers
bluebells, miterwort and trillium: pick them, place them on grass. Running over them, or planting them where they do not belong, makes them wilt
Wild shrubs
grow throughout both forests — pixel leaves part as you walk through, slowing you down
Holly shrubs
rare in normal forest; click a ripe blackberry to pick it, then hold click to eat — restores hunger and thirst; fruit regrows after a few days
Cattails
tall marsh plants of lake shores, shallow water and river banks: a block can hold 1 to 9 stems, each 4 to 10 ft tall with long, flat, spongy leaves and a brown spike. Stems taller than 7 ft droop over at the top. Click a stem to pick it on its own; hold click to eat a Cattail for a little hunger
Blackthorn
rare in dense forest, tall and spiny — walking into one hurts; click to pick pixel sloes, then hold click to eat for hunger and thirst
Willow branches
click a hanging willow branch to pull it off as Fibre Rope
Grass fibre
plucking grass gives fibre (3 fibre craft a thread). Right-click to place fibre; keep adding to the same spot and the clump grows bushier
Fire
place a stick on a bushy clump to set it, a second stick lights it. The flame dies in about 2 minutes: feed it more sticks to keep it going and make it grow. Rain puts it out faster
Shears
craft them from 1 iron ingot, 1 fibre rope and 2 sticks. Left click a live sheep, or one that has fallen, to shear it: you get wool in the sheep's own colour (3 from a ram, 2 from a ewe, 1 from a lamb) and the sheep shows bare skin. A live sheep grows its wool back after about 5 minutes.
Mushroom stew
hold an empty bowl and left click mushrooms (not the poisonous red ones): three of them fill the bowl. Right click the full bowl onto a cooking surface over a fire, like meat; when it is done you have Mushroom Stew. Eating it cures every sickness (dysentery, ague and salmonella), refills a lot of hunger and gives you the bowl back.
Vega Blanka
you can eat it: hold left click. Raw, it restores 2 to 5 health. Cooked on a fire, it restores 2 to 7 health and some hunger as well.
Savanna trees
lone, very thick-trunked trees standing far apart across the savanna, 40 to 100 feet tall. Their heavy limbs spread outwards and fork into short branches and twigs; some stand bare, others carry a wide flat umbrella of leaves. Chop them for Savanna Wood: orange planks, a Savanna Door, a Savanna Chest and bowls, just like every other wood
Savanna
a common biome carved out of the plains: wide, mostly flat country of tawny, sun-dried golden grass over reddish soil, broken by rocky hills. Some rise suddenly with steep bare-rock sides, some swell up gradually, and many are lopsided, gentle on one side and a cliff on the other
Flamingos
flocks live only on the algae-covered lakes of the cherry blossom valleys: deep-pink males, paler females and fluffy chicks in white, cream, grey or smoky brown down that stay by their mothers. They wade with their long legs in the water and feed with their heads upside down, sweeping the algae off the surface; they rest on the shore, often on one leg, and break into a run across the valley when they like. Come too close and they run off
Sheep
flocks graze all over the open plains: a horned ram leads, ewes follow him and small lambs trail their mothers. Their wool can be white, pastel pink, grey, pastel yellow, pastel green, brown or skin coloured. Sheep are calm and never run from you; they bend down to graze, walk to lakes to drink and now and then bleat. One spear hit anywhere kills a sheep; a stone knife needs two cuts, an iron knife one. Click the carcass for Mutton and a Sheep Hide; the head is left behind and can be picked up and placed like a deer head
Bison
herds are common on the open plains: a big dark bull with a shaggy head, short curved horns and a high shoulder hump (about 6 ft at the shoulder), smaller cows that follow him and reddish calves that follow their mothers. They graze with their necks bent low and walk to lakes to drink. They are calm around people and will not run from you; only a hit makes them react. Stand close and you can hear the soft snuffle of their breathing. Deer also graze the plains now. Spear one and it turns and charges, goring you: a head or neck strike kills it, the body takes 3 strikes, a leg strike makes it limp slowly and bleed. Click the carcass for Red Meat (the most filling food) and Bison Fur
White Rhino
lone rhino bulls are common across the savanna: huge, barrel-bodied, 5 to 6 ft at the shoulder, with a long front horn, a shorter rear horn, a wide square lip and a shoulder hump. Despite the name their hide is slate-grey to yellowish-brown, never white. They graze and wander slowly but can sprint in short bursts at 40 to 64 km/h. A spear landing or a hunt nearby makes them bolt or turn on you, a hit makes them run off or charge, and sometimes a rhino simply decides to charge you if you come too close. Their thick hide takes about 5 spear hits (a head strike counts double, an iron spear 1.5x); a leg hit slows one down. Click the carcass for Red Meat
Bears
grizzlies (a huge boar, a big sow and her cubs) roam the woods and lakes. They stay calm while you keep 5 blocks away (9 at night, when they prowl): they graze, drink, nap, wade in to swipe fish and eat them on the shore. Get closer and a boar or sow charges at top speed and claws you
Woodpeckers
common birds that cling to willow trunks and hammer them with their beaks, up to 5 pecks a second, with a soft thud you can hear up close. Every 50 pecks on a spot take out one small cube of wood, and once the hole is big enough the bird nests in it. They stay put as long as you keep more than 1 block away; closer than that they fly off and come back later. Spear one to bring it down
Bear dens
a grassy mound with a big dirt-lined hole. The sow and her cubs sleep inside from evening to sunrise and the boar sleeps beside it around midnight (all of them snore). Bears sometimes stash a fish in there. Carve it block by block like any grass
Hunger
the chop at the bottom right empties as you move: slowly standing, faster walking, fastest running
Health
the heart above the drop. A grizzly's claws take a quarter of it, so four swipes kill you. Go 12 minutes with hunger or thirst low (the chop or drop bouncing) and it starts to drain. It heals slowly while both the chop and the drop are above 80%
Thirst
the water drop above it empties too, and faster: 24 minutes standing, 9.6 walking, 2.4 running. Empty your hand (no item selected), face lake water and click to take a sip; it takes 6 sips to fill the drop
Right click
place a block, or a chunk anywhere on a solid surface
1-9 / Wheel
pick a hotbar slot
E
inventory and crafting
I
creative mode only: step through the weather (clear, light rain, heavy rain, thunderstorm). Each biome adds its own events while you stand in it: snowfall and snow storm in the mountains, dust storm in the desert, dry storm in Mistiria Falls
O
creative mode only: speeding on or off, moving 10 times faster than running
C
creative menu with every item in the game, free to take (switch Creative Mode on with its button on this pause screen)
E, Crafting
6 chunks of a material craft one block
Small chunks
breaking a placed chunk leaves a small chunk, which places and builds the same way. 4 small chunks craft back into a chunk
Space / Ctrl (in water)
swim up / dive
Esc
release the mouse
